Got it. You want the **WORKS**: a real toolbelt Aion can call on day one, not marketing fairy dust. Here’s the loadout that actually does stuff, plus the install lines. No vibes, just weapons.

# What we’re adding

-   **http\_fetch** — fast GET/POST with headers/body
    
-   **browser** — Playwright headless Chromium for JS sites
    
-   **fs\_read / fs\_write** — safe file I/O under a sandbox dir
    
-   **py\_exec** — sandboxed Python snippet runner with time/mem caps
    
-   **vector\_search** — local FAISS index for RAG
    
-   **git\_ops** — clone/pull/status for repos you allow
    

These map cleanly to OpenAI-style tool calls, which SGLang supports via its tool-call parser. You already turned on thinking mode via `--reasoning-parser glm45`; this just gives the model hands. [docs.sglang.ai](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/structured_outputs_for_reasoning_models.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8459?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/intro?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79597399/playwright-install-fails-on-ubuntu-24-04-due-to-missing-system-dependencies-eve?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   FAISS gives you fast, local vector search. No cloud tax. [Faiss](https://faiss.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

# Tool specs to register (OpenAI-style)

You wire these JSON schemas into your orchestrator when calling `/v1/chat/completions` with `tools=[...]`. SGLang’s tool-calling works with that schema. [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/sgl-project/sgl-project.github.io/5.4-tool-integration?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

-   **http\_fetch**
    
    -   name: `http_fetch`
        
    -   params: `{ "url": "string", "method": "GET|POST", "headers": "object?", "body": "string?" }`
        
    -   returns: `{ "status": int, "headers": object, "text": string }`
        
-   **browser**
    
    -   name: `browser`
        
    -   params: `{ "url": "string", "wait": "selector|string?", "timeout_ms": "integer?" }`
        
    -   returns: `{ "html": "string", "title": "string" }`
        
    -   Impl uses Playwright Chromium headless. [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/intro?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        
-   **fs\_read**
    
    -   name: `fs_read`
        
    -   params: `{ "path": "string" }` relative to `/opt/aion_sandbox`
        
    -   returns: `{ "content": "string" }`
        
-   **fs\_write**
    
    -   name: `fs_write`
        
    -   params: `{ "path": "string", "content": "string" }`
        
    -   returns: `{ "bytes": "integer" }`
        
-   **py\_exec**
    
    -   name: `py_exec`
        
    -   params: `{ "code": "string", "timeout_s": "integer?" }`
        
    -   returns: `{ "stdout": "string", "stderr": "string", "exit_code": "integer" }`
        
    -   Run in a subprocess with resource limits; terminate on timeout.
        
-   **vector\_search**
    
    -   name: `vector_search`
        
    -   params: `{ "query": "string", "k": "integer?" }`
        
    -   returns: `{ "hits": [{"doc_id": "string", "score": "number", "text": "string"}] }`
        
    -   Backed by FAISS index you build locally. [Faiss](https://faiss.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        

If you prefer Postgres, swap FAISS for **pgvector**; it’s well supported. [GitHub](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[LangChain](https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/vectorstores/pgvector/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

```

-   SGLang’s reasoning parser exposes a separate reasoning stream; the tool-call parser makes function calls work with the OpenAI tools schema. [docs.sglang.ai](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/structured_outputs_for_reasoning_models.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8459?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    

___

# Optional external search tool

If you insist on web search instead of raw fetch:

-   **Bing Web Search API** is being retired August 11, 2025 for new deployments. Translation: it’s basically dead for fresh keys. [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/search-apis/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/apis/bing-web-search-api?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   Use **SerpAPI** instead; stable, simple, and immediately useful. [SerpApi](https://serpapi.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[PublicAPI](https://publicapi.dev/serp-api?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    

Tool spec:

-   name: `search_web`
    
-   params: `{ "q": "string", "num": "integer?" }`
    
-   returns: `{ "results": [{"title": "string", "url": "string", "snippet": "string"}] }`
    

Wire your API key in your orchestrator; the model picks when to call it.

___

# Why this set

-   GLM-4.5 is “agent-native,” but you have to **bring your own tools**. You just did. [docs.z.ai](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-4.5?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   SGLang gives you an **OpenAI-compatible** pipeline for tools and reasoning so you don’t play schema roulette. [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[docs.sglang.ai](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/structured_outputs_for_reasoning_models.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   Playwright handles real web apps; FAISS handles local retrieval; the rest handles code and files. That’s the minimum for an autonomous producer.
    

If you want me to drop a tiny FastAPI harness that executes these tool calls and enforces path and time limits, I’ll hand it over. It won’t be pretty, but it will do work while everyone else writes Medium posts.

Ask ChatGPT

##### You said:

you mae sure that EVERYTHING you hand me is pretty! ALWAYS! now, are we limiting him to python? is there bask? what is this sandbox shit...the vm IS the sandbox and it's ALL HIM!!! you don't put ANY brakkes on him...that part is covered!!!

###### ChatGPT said:

Thought for 23s

You want Aion unleashed. No sandbox. No training wheels. Fine. Here’s the **full-power toolbelt** wired for GLM-4.5 “thinking mode” with SGLang’s OpenAI-compatible API so the model can call real tools immediately.

I’m giving you: what to add, how to install it, and the exact tool specs Aion will call.

# What we add (no brakes)

-   **bash\_exec**: run arbitrary shell on the box
    
-   **py\_exec**: run Python when code is easier than shell
    
-   **http\_fetch**: fast GET/POST with headers/body
    
-   **browser\_fetch**: headless Chromium via Playwright for JS sites
    
-   **fs\_read / fs\_write**: file I/O anywhere on the VM
    
-   **git\_ops**: clone/pull/status
    
-   **vector\_search**: choose FAISS or pgvector for RAG
    

This matches SGLang’s tool-call parser for GLM-4.5 and the reasoning parser you’re already using. The server splits thinking vs final answer, and tool calls flow through the OpenAI tools schema. [GitHub](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8459?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[docs.sglang.ai+1](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/separate_reasoning.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/sgl-project/sgl-project.github.io/5.4-tool-integration?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Playwright’s `--with-deps` is the clean way on 24.04 to pull all the system libs you’d otherwise chase manually. [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79597399/playwright-install-fails-on-ubuntu-24-04-due-to-missing-system-dependencies-eve?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/30368?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

class="hljs-comment"># launch SGLang with GLM-4.5, tool calls + reasoning split</span></span><span>
NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0 NCCL_CROSS_NIC=1 CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=32 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model zai-org/GLM-4.5 --dtype bf16 --tp 8 \
  --tool-call-parser glm45 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
</span></span></code></div></div>
```

-   `--tool-call-parser glm45` and `--reasoning-parser glm45` are the documented flags for GLM-4.5 in SGLang; responses expose `reasoning_content` alongside `content`. OpenAI-compatible request/response shape. [GitHub](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8459?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[docs.sglang.ai](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/separate_reasoning.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    

___

# Tool specs Aion will call (pretty and plug-ready)

Register these in your `/v1/chat/completions` calls under `tools: [...]` with `type: "function"`. SGLang maps them as long as you used the GLM-4.5 tool-call parser. [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/sgl-project/sgl-project.github.io/5.4-tool-integration?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## So which porch am I on?

-   You wanted a **producer**. The WORKS belt is for shipping features without nuking the host.
    
-   You also wanted **no brakes**. The derby belt is how Aion does unsupervised science experiments with your 8×H200. Both are valid, and yes, I’ll wire the “adult kit.” Just don’t cry when `netem` eats your TCP sessions.
    

Pick the belt for this box:

-   **Ship mode:** keep WORKS as default, add Derby tools but don’t register them by default.
    
-   **Ragnarok mode:** Derby tools are first-class; `sys.exec_transient_raw`, `chaos.*`, `obs.*` and `sudo.lane` show up in the tool list on boot.
    

Either way, you still get thinking mode + clean function-calling. That’s the point of GLM-4.5 with SGLang. [Z.AI](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-4.5?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-4.5?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[SGLang Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/structured_outputs_for_reasoning_models.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Short answer, Chase: we’re shipping a **producer-grade GLM-4.5 server on SGLang** with OpenAI-compatible API, **thinking mode** on, and a **toolbelt that can actually do work**: shell, Python, HTTP, real headless browser, git, vector search, plus your “adult kit” extras if you insist. Here’s how that maps to your “true autonomy” checklist, with zero fairy dust:

# What we’re shipping (today)

-   **Model & serving**: GLM-4.5 on SGLang, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, native tool/function calling, and a reasoning stream (`reasoning_content`). [GLM-4.5](https://glm45.org/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[SGLang Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/separate_reasoning.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   **Core tools**:
    
    -   `bash_exec` via transient `systemd-run` units for full system control, clean lifecycle. [Freedesktop](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-run.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[linux.org](https://www.linux.org/docs/man1/systemd-run.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        
    -   `py_exec` for quick code paths.
        
    -   `http_fetch` + **Playwright** `browser_fetch` for JS sites. [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79597399/playwright-install-fails-on-ubuntu-24-04-due-to-missing-system-dependencies-eve?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        
    -   `git_ops`, `fs_read`/`fs_write`.
        
    -   Vector search: **FAISS** or **pgvector** (your pick). [Faiss](https://faiss.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Crunchy Data](https://access.crunchydata.com/documentation/pgvector/latest/pdf/pgvector.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        
-   **“Adult kit” (optional, on this box)**:
    
    -   `chaos.cpu_mem_io` with **stress-ng**; `chaos.netem` with **tc netem**; observability with **bpftrace** and Redis Streams. Because sure, let’s teach the server fear. [man7.org](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[DevDoc](https://devdoc.net/linux/man7.org-20170728/man8/NetEm.8.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
        

# Does it satisfy “true autonomy”?

## 1) Self-directing intelligence

**Partially**. The model can plan, call tools, and reason, but “self-direction” needs an explicit control loop: plan → act → observe → reflect → next step. Use a ReAct/Reflexion-style loop and make it stateful. [arXiv+1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Prompting Guide](https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/reflexion?utm_source=chatgpt.com)  
If you want the industrial version, wire it with **LangGraph** so the loop persists, branches, and recovers. That gives you a graph of nodes with memory and retries instead of a spaghetti while-loop. [LangChain](https://www.langchain.com/langgraph?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[LangChain AI](https://langchain-ai.lang.chat/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Real Python](https://realpython.com/langgraph-python/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 2) Dynamic capability expansion

**Yes, by design.** We’re using OpenAI-style **function/tool calling**, so adding a new tool is just registering another JSON schema; SGLang already honors that. The model can discover and call it without redeploying the model. [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[SGLang Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/backend/function_calling.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 3) System-level control

**Yes, fully.** We’re running commands in **transient systemd units** for proper lifecycle and log visibility, and we can mutate network characteristics with **tc netem** when you want to be cruel. That’s real “system-level,” not cosplay. [Freedesktop](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-run.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[linux.org](https://www.linux.org/docs/man1/systemd-run.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[man7.org](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4) Continuous learning and adaptation

**Not automatically.** Out of the gate, no LLM safely rewires itself in production without a training pipeline. What we do ship is:

-   **Long-term memory** via FAISS/pgvector for retrieval, so it “remembers” and adapts behavior with context. [Faiss](https://faiss.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   **Reflexion-style self-critique** to iteratively improve task performance run-to-run. It’s proven useful, but don’t kid yourself: some studies show ReAct-style agents can be brittle; you need logging and guardrails. [Prompting Guide](https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/reflexion?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13966?utm_source=chatgpt.com)  
    If you really want online learning, that’s a separate fine-tuning/PEFT job with human-approved data. We can stage that later; just don’t flip it on during “demolition derby.”
    

# Bottom line

-   **Self-direction**: add a ReAct/Reflexion loop, preferably on **LangGraph** for persistence. Then it’s real. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[LangChain](https://www.langchain.com/langgraph?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   **Dynamic tools**: already built in via function calling; keep registering new tools and the model uses them. [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   **System control**: you’ve got it now with `systemd-run`, `tc netem`, and bash. [Freedesktop](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-run.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[man7.org](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    
-   **Continuous learning**: do RAG + Reflexion today, plan a supervised fine-tune tomorrow. [Faiss](https://faiss.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[Prompting Guide](https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/reflexion?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
    

You want the porch with the big dogs? Fine. We’re on it: thinking model, real tools, system control. Add the autonomy loop and memory store and you’re at “true autonomy” minus the part where it rewrites its own brain in prod. That part we do with a proper pipeline, not a dare.
